litigation.note: A single long-running share-transfer dispute. Under 'Significant and material orders passed by the Regulators or Courts', the Directors' Report records that in 2018 an ex-shareholder, Ms. Dimple Khetan, filed suit before the NCLT Ahmedabad against the Company, Promoters and then directors under sections 58, 59 and 213 of the Companies Act, 2013; on 28 November 2024 the NCLT ordered rectification of the register of members restoring her as owner of 28,000 equity shares (56,000 after bonus), and the buyers and the Company have appealed, with the matter now sub judice before the NCLAT, New Delhi. The complaints disclosure adds that SEBI disposed of her complaint, the ROC found no violation or error in the transaction, and a related matter is sub judice at the Andheri court with charges not yet framed. The Company characterises it as a matter between buyer and seller in which directors and promoters have no role, with no material financial or operational impact on its business or going-concern status; no amount or provision is disclosed. Otherwise the Company states there are no significant material orders affecting going concern, and no application or proceeding is pending under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

risks.note: Management's own first-listed challenge: 'The agricultural sector remains exposed to unseasonal rainfall, heat waves, changes in monsoon patterns, crop disease and water shortages. These factors can affect production volume, product quality, procurement prices and continuity of supply.' The MD's message confirms this bit in FY2025-26, with erratic weather, unseasonal rainfall and extreme temperatures affecting production and availability across several crop-growing regions.

Management states that 'a substantial increase in physical volume may not translate into proportionate revenue growth when the product mix shifts towards lower-priced commodities or market prices decline. Managing the balance between throughput and realisation is therefore a key operating challenge.' This is live rather than theoretical: FY2025-26 outward volume rose 97.1% to 65,132 MT against 24.0% standalone revenue growth, with onions the principal throughput driver (standalone onion volumes up approximately 147.9%), and the business review explicitly cites 'lower blended realisations'.
risks.risk: Lower and volatile realisations — throughput growth need not convert to revenue

risks.note: Management flags that 'growth in institutional, organised retail, export and HORECA channels can lead to higher receivables and longer credit periods. The Company must fund farmer and supplier payments while awaiting collection from customers.' The MD&A adds that the increase in receivables and borrowings 'highlights the need for continued focus on customer credit evaluation, collection efficiency and working-capital discipline', and the MD's message places working-capital efficiency and cash conversion at the centre of future value creation.

'Fresh fruits and vegetables have limited shelf lives. Delays in procurement, storage, transportation or customer offtake can result in quality deterioration and commercial losses.' Shelf life caps how much inventory risk the business can carry and makes execution timing, not just sourcing price, a determinant of margin.

'Geopolitical developments, changes in tariffs, import regulations, export restrictions and freight availability can affect international demand and supply-chain economics.' This bears directly on the export channel the Company is expanding (currently exporting to 6 countries), and the outlook adds that export and HORECA demand may remain uneven.

'Fuel and transportation represent important components of the cost structure. An increase in oil prices may increase freight, refrigeration and distribution costs.' The outlook repeats that higher oil prices could increase transportation and logistics costs — a direct margin exposure for a business whose value-add is physical movement and cold storage.

'Cluster development, food processing, cold-chain infrastructure and contract-farming initiatives involve capital, regulatory approvals, partner coordination and utilisation risk.' The proposed Nashik Peri-Urban Vegetables Cluster (approximately Rs.124.28 crore total, of which approximately Rs.74.53 crore is the Company's Implementing Agency share) is still a proposal, with NHB assistance of up to approximately Rs.24.46 crore 'subject to appraisal, sanction, achievement of prescribed milestones and compliance with programme guidelines' and no commissioning timeline disclosed, while land at Sinnar Taluka has already been acquired.

'The industry includes local traders, wholesalers, logistics companies, organised supply-chain platforms, food processors and large retailers with direct-sourcing operations.' Management separately flags that 'the entry of large, venture-backed agri-tech and food-tech start-ups with significant capital resources and aggressive expansion strategies poses a competitive threat, especially in key urban and export markets' — the same channels (quick commerce, modern retail, exports) the Company is scaling into.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity and entry of well-funded agri-tech start-ups

currentContext.expansion: Prime Fresh's principal announced expansion is the proposed integrated Peri-Urban Vegetables Cluster at the Nashik Urban Centre, submitted under the National Horticulture Board's Cluster Development Programme and described in the report as a proposal rather than a sanctioned or commissioned project. The catchment covers approximately 50-100 kilometres around Nashik with focus areas across Niphad, Sinnar, Satana and Malegaon, and a crop basket spanning onion, tomato, cauliflower, cabbage, capsicum, sweet corn, green peas, gourds, okra, brinjal, chillies, cucumber, beans, leafy and root vegetables plus grapes, pomegranate, banana and guava. The proposal envisages total investment of approximately Rs.124.28 crore, of which the Implementing Agency (Prime Fresh) component is approximately Rs.74.53 crore to be deployed across post-harvest management infrastructure, technology, marketing, nursery development, farmer and FPO development and logistics vehicles with a retail model; eligible NHB assistance is proposed at up to approximately Rs.24.46 crore, subject to appraisal, sanction, milestone achievement and programme compliance. Proposed physical components comprise farmer and production interventions across approximately 5,215 hectares with training for around 8,500 farmers, two collection and aggregation centres, one integrated packhouse and fourteen farm-gate packhouses, a 6,000 MT multi-commodity cold-storage facility and approximately 3,000 MT of frozen storage, ten refrigerated vehicles with crates, pallets and handling infrastructure, an Individual Quick Freezing line of 3 MT per hour, a dehydration unit of 2 tonnes per day, a blast freezer of 1 MT per batch, and technology systems for farm management, remote sensing, traceability, market intelligence, procurement, inventory and customer management. No commissioning or completion timeline is disclosed for any of these components. Supporting this direction, the Company acquired strategic land in Sinnar Taluka, Nashik District, Maharashtra during FY2025-26 to support long-term growth in sourcing, post-harvest infrastructure and value-added agriculture, and was ranked No. 1 across all three Expressions of Interest submitted under the NHB Cluster Development Programme with scores of 42 to 46 out of 50. On the existing footprint, the Company states it has built operational capacity of more than 5.5 lakh tonnes per annum across inward handling, outward dispatch, sorting, grading, packing, cleaning, loading and unloading, and it commenced new distribution centre operations in Lucknow during the year. The Directors' Report records no change in the nature of business during FY2025-26.

moat.body:
- Backward-integrated sourcing ecosystem: engagement with more than 1,30,000+ farmers across production clusters, 100+ FPO partners, relationships with 90+ APMCs and 2,400 suppliers and local aggregators, providing reliable market linkages and assured prompt payment to farmers
- Omni-channel distribution model that allocates produce across modern trade, e-commerce/quick commerce, HORECA, processors, exports and general trade based on quality, volume, shelf life, pricing, credit profile and demand — reducing dependence on any single customer segment and improving supply-chain …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management's own first-listed challenge: 'The agricultural sector remains exposed to unseasonal rainfall, heat waves, changes in monsoon patterns, crop disease and water shortages. These factors can affect production volume, product quality, procurement prices and continuity of supply.' The MD's message confirms this bit in FY2025-26, with erratic weather, unseasonal rainfall and extreme temperatures affecting production and availability across several crop-growing regions.
- Management states that 'a substantial increase in physical volume may not translate into proportionate revenue growth when the product mix shifts towards lower-priced commodities or market prices decline. Managing the balance between throughput and realisation is therefore a key operating challenge.' This is live rather than theoretical: FY2025-26 outward volume rose 97.1% to 65,132 MT against 24.0% standalone revenue growth, with onions the principal throughput driver (standalone onion volumes up approximately 147.9%), and the business review explicitly cites 'lower blended realisations'.
- Management flags that 'growth in institutional, organised retail, export and HORECA channels can lead to higher receivables and longer credit periods. The Company must fund farmer and supplier payments while awaiting collection from customers.' The MD&A adds that the increase in receivables and borrowings 'highlights the need for continued focus on customer credit evaluation, collection efficiency and working-capital discipline', and the MD's message places working-capital efficiency and cash conversion at the centre of future value creation.
- 'Fresh fruits and vegetables have limited shelf lives. Delays in procurement, storage, transportation or customer offtake can result in quality deterioration and commercial losses.' Shelf life caps how much inventory risk the business can carry and makes execution timing, not just sourcing price, a determinant of margin.
- 'Geopolitical developments, changes in tariffs, import regulations, export restrictions and freight availability can affect international demand and supply-chain economics.' This bears directly on the export channel the Company is expanding (currently exporting to 6 countries), and the outlook adds that export and HORECA demand may remain uneven.
- 'Fuel and transportation represent important components of the cost structure. An increase in oil prices may increase freight, refrigeration and distribution costs.' The outlook repeats that higher oil prices could increase transportation and logistics costs — a direct margin exposure for a business whose value-add is physical movement and cold storage.
- 'Cluster development, food processing, cold-chain infrastructure and contract-farming initiatives involve capital, regulatory approvals, partner coordination and utilisation risk.' The proposed Nashik Peri-Urban Vegetables Cluster (approximately Rs.124.28 crore total, of which approximately Rs.74.53 crore is the Company's Implementing Agency share) is still a proposal, with NHB assistance of up to approximately Rs.24.46 crore 'subject to appraisal, sanction, achievement of prescribed milestones and compliance with programme guidelines' and no commissioning timeline disclosed, while land at Sinnar Taluka has already been acquired.
- 'The industry includes local traders, wholesalers, logistics companies, organised supply-chain platforms, food processors and large retailers with direct-sourcing operations.' Management separately flags that 'the entry of large, venture-backed agri-tech and food-tech start-ups with significant capital resources and aggressive expansion strategies poses a competitive threat, especially in key urban and export markets' — the same channels (quick commerce, modern retail, exports) the Company is scaling into.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Evolve from a fresh fruits and vegetables sourcing and distribution company into an integrated agri value-chain platform — management's stated objective is to move from a strong fresh-produce supply chain into a future-ready, technology-driven, sustainable agricultural enterprise.
- Pursue cluster-led infrastructure development under the National Horticulture Board's Cluster Development Programme, anchored by the proposed integrated Peri-Urban Vegetables Cluster at the Nashik Urban Centre covering a 50-100 km catchment across Niphad, Sinnar, Satana and Malegaon.
- Increase capacity utilisation …

hero.oneLiner: Prime Fresh Limited is an Ahmedabad-headquartered, fully integrated agri value-chain company in post-harvest management and distribution of fruits and vegetables, with over 19+ years of operating experience connecting farmers and production clusters with organised domestic and international markets.
